sections.name: lesson
sections.title: Plain-English lesson sentence
sections.what: Writes one sentence comparing the best option with the runner-up, or a coin flip note when no grade is given.
sections.why: The code comment says it is template-based with no language model.
sections.watch_out: If the options are tied or missing, the sentence is blank.

sections.name: ReviewPage (part 1)
sections.title: Verdict and sign-in
sections.what: Requires sign-in and loads the review, or shows a no-call message. Records the view, prepares figures, and draws the verdict with the pick, confidence, points, rating change and calibration, or a coin flip message.
sections.why: The verdict puts the grade first, so the fan sees the result before the detail.
sections.watch_out: The rating is shown as before and after values. If the service changes their order, the text would read backwards.

sections.name: ReviewPage (part 2)
sections.title: Review columns, chart and links
sections.what: Draws three columns: what happened (from ball data), what was reasonable beforehand (model estimates), and a labelled what-if. Then draws a win chance chart, the lesson, and links to the next read and the share card.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps facts, estimates and what-ifs visibly separate.
sections.watch_out: The chart's ghost points use the fixed 120 ball scale, and the share card link appears only for graded calls.

summary: Shows a fan's review of one of their calls: the pick, its grade, what happened, what was reasonable, and a clearly labelled what-if estimate.
purpose: Helps fans learn from their calls by separating facts from estimates.
why: The labels say facts, model estimates and what-ifs are shown separately. Other reasons are not stated.
how: Requires sign-in and loads the review. If there is no call, shows a no-call message. Otherwise records a view and prepares the figures, then draws the verdict, three columns (what happened, what was reasonable, what might have happened otherwise), a win chance chart, a lesson sentence, and links to the next read and a share card.
inputs: Moment id, the signed-in user, the review data from reviewCall, and the next moment from nextMomentFor.
outputs: A review page with the grade, three columns, a chart, a lesson and links.
risks: Points and percentages depend on correct model output. The timeline assumes 120 balls, which fits T20 only. The share card link shows only for graded calls.
debug: If the grade is missing, check reviewCall and the grade fields. If the lesson is blank, check the best and second options. If the chart looks off, check the 120 ball assumption.
